prompt: A realistic 1920s photograph on grainy colour film: real people with real skin, pores and stubble. The whole frame is seen through the thick faceted bottom of a cut-crystal whiskey glass held up to the lens: the room is split into a dozen overlapping copies, each shifted, each edged with thin rainbow fringes. Camera at table height in a hidden speakeasy back room. Gangsters in pinstripes and a tall skinny man in a bowler hat with a heavy gold mayoral chain round his neck, a long narrow face, hollow cheeks and a pencil-thin grey moustache sit at a green-baize poker table piled with chips, banknotes and whole hams, cigars in their mouths, frozen mid-deal, all turned to the open door, where a heavy-set Black man in his fifties with a shaved head, a broken nose and a double chin, in a sweat-stained vest, flour on his forearms stands holding one small loaf. Light: one low brass lamp with a green glass shade over the table pooling amber; the doorway cold blue behind the baker; cigar smoke in flat layers. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
